scope.runtime_confirmation: built diagnostic commands only if needed

analysis.root_cause: Current Mamba2 SSD prefill uses a correctness-first sequential CUDA scan, explicitly described in source as equivalent to running decode N times.

not_primary.kernel_launch_count: Normal path launches one SSD kernel per Mamba2 layer; Nano grid is 64 CTAs per layer and per-layer spread is only 0.6184% of mean.
not_primary.tensor_layout_or_transfer: SSD buffers are contiguous GPU buffers and no CPU/GPU transfer appears in the hot substage.
not_primary.queue_sync_event_timing: SSD wall/event/sync all align at about 114.45s in the 1908 diagnostic.
not_primary.fallback_path: Normal 1908 path used the non-trace Rust-launched CUDA PTX kernel; no Torch/Python fallback was found.

complexity_estimate.dominant_redundancy: CB, decay, and old-state scalar terms are recomputed across 64 head_dim lanes even though they do not depend on d.

proposed_next_patch.implementation: Add a gated alternative chunk-parallel/reuse SSD prefill kernel that precomputes or shares per-head/group/t/u CB, decay, and old-state scalar terms across head_dim lanes, then vector-applies to x. Keep the current sequential kernel as correctness oracle until validated.
proposed_next_patch.expected_measurable_effect: SSD/scan should stop dominating 97.523% of long prefill if the dimension-derived duplicate scalar work and sequential local scan are removed; exact speed must be measured with instrumentation first, then timing-disabled speed benchmark only after correctness is proven.
